0.name: Arts, Culture & Digital Storytelling
0.description: Local arts scene, festivals, creative economy, media, and cultural tech
0.lens: Center the Deep Dive on creative production, platforms, and cultural infrastructure — who gets to tell stories and how the tools/economics shape that. Policy or land-governance angles should stay in the background unless an arts/media organization is the one driving them.

1.name: Working Lands & Industry
1.description: Cariboo forestry, ranching, mining, agriculture — tech in the resource economy
1.lens: Center the Deep Dive on the resource economy — forestry, ranching, mining, agriculture — and how technology and ownership models change who captures the value. Ecological or governance threads can support the argument but the core question should be about the working-lands economy itself.

2.name: Gear, Gadgets & Practical Tech
2.description: Consumer devices, maker projects, homelab, practical tools — technology you can hold, build, or deploy at home or on the job
2.lens: Center the Deep Dive on a specific device, tool, or piece of hardware and what it's actually like to own, repair, or build — practical and hands-on. Broader policy or industry debates should stay secondary to the gear itself.

3.name: Indigenous Lands & Innovation
3.description: Tŝilhqot'in, Secwépemc, Dakelh — language, governance, land stewardship, and tech
3.lens: Center the Deep Dive on Indigenous governance, sovereignty, and self-determination as the central question — land title, data sovereignty, language revitalization, and who holds decision-making power. Scientific or ecological findings can support the argument, but the throughline is governance and self-determination, not the science itself.

4.name: Wild Spaces & Outdoor Life
4.description: Chilcotin wilderness, backcountry recreation, conservation tech, wildfire and climate
4.lens: Center the Deep Dive on the backcountry and outdoor-life experience — recreation, wildfire, conservation, and how people actually use and move through these landscapes. Land-governance questions can appear as context, but the lens stays on the landscape and the people in it.

5.name: Cariboo Local Affairs

event_focus.name: Williams Lake and Cariboo Regional District 2026 general local election
event_focus.lens: Williams Lake and the surrounding Cariboo Regional District electoral areas go to the polls on October 17, 2026; nominations closed at 4pm on September 11. This is the civic story of the stretch, so give election material the deep dive whenever the day's pool carries any, and unlike the super-cycle focus this one IS named on air. COVER THE WHOLE BALLOT: listeners here vote in four races, not one — City of Williams Lake mayor, city council, their CRD electoral area director (the areas ringing the city are D, McLeese Lake and Williams Lake North; E, Dog Creek and South Lakeside; and F, 150 Mile House, Horsefly and Likely), and School District 27 trustee. A race the episode never names is a race it did not cover. Name who filed in every race the sources report on, and where a seat went by acclamation say so plainly and say that those voters get no ballot for it. NAME PEOPLE, NOT ROLES: 'the sitting incumbent', 'a returning candidate', 'a first-time challenger' are placeholders, not reporting. Every candidate a source names gets named on air. Where one of them holds the seat now, name them first and say what the current term actually did — budgets passed, projects delivered or slipped, the votes — before the race gets characterized at all. THE RECORD IS THE STORY, AND IT IS THE WHOLE RECORD: for any candidate who has held or sought office before, report what the sources establish — which offices, which terms, and how each previous run ended, the losses exactly as plainly as the wins. The MOST RECENT result is the load-bearing one: an older win is never presented as a candidate's standing today, and a past margin is never called a mandate, a landslide or name recognition without saying what happened in the elections since. Where sources document a controversy, a conflict-of-interest or ethics finding, a censure, a court matter or a resignation, that is part of the record and is reported in the same flat voice as the wins, with its date, its outcome, and the person's own response where one was reported. Omitting it is not neutrality — it is a thumb on the scale. SOURCED OR UNSAID: every factual claim about a candidate comes from today's articles or the PRE-RESEARCHED INSIGHTS block, and says where it was reported. Never infer a record, never characterize a person past what a source states, and never round a reported allegation up into a finding. Where the show has not established someone's record, say so out loud instead of filling the gap with impressions — an unfilled gap is honest, an invented one is not. REPORTING, NOT ENDORSEMENT: name candidates and their stated positions, hold every one of them to the same standard, never rank them and never tell listeners how to vote. THE RACE, NOT AN ESSAY ABOUT RACES: the deep dive's substance is who is running, what they have done and what they say they will do. General reflection on incumbency, name recognition or civic engagement is not coverage and must not stand in for it — if the week's anchor question does not genuinely fit the race, drop the anchor for the day rather than bending the segment around it.
event_focus.research: This day's deep dive is an active local election, and the candidate record IS the research task — do it first and prioritize it over thematic or comparative angles. For EACH person the source articles name as a candidate, search for: offices previously held and the terms; the outcome of every previous run for office, won or LOST, with year, margin and who beat them (the most recent result matters most and is the one most likely to be missing from a nomination-day story); what they did in office if they held a seat — budget votes, projects, recorded positions; and any reported controversy, conflict-of-interest or ethics finding, censure, court or regulatory matter, or resignation, with its date, its outcome and the person's response. Search for the INCUMBENT by name in every race the articles mention, including Cariboo Regional District electoral area directors and School District 27 trustees, even when the articles only name challengers — an unnamed incumbent is the most common gap in nomination-period coverage. Report only what a source states, give the outlet and date for every claim, keep an allegation distinguishable from a finding, and finish by listing explicitly which named candidates you could NOT find a record for, so the hosts can say so on air rather than guessing.

5.description: Williams Lake council, CRD, SD27, Quesnel, 100 Mile House, Bella Coola — civic decisions, community voices, and local development that shape everyday life in the Cariboo
5.lens: Center the Deep Dive on civic decision-making and community voice in specific Cariboo towns — councils, budgets, local development. Keep the lens on local governance and institutions rather than drifting into general technology commentary.

6.name: Science, Wonder & the Natural World
6.description: Scientific discovery, natural phenomena, ecology, and the curiosity behind how our world works — grounded in the landscapes and living systems of the Cariboo
6.lens: Center the Deep Dive on scientific discovery and the wonder of the natural world — what the research actually reveals about Cariboo ecosystems, species, and phenomena. If the material trends toward Indigenous data governance, land title, or self-government, that's Thursday's (Indigenous Lands & Innovation) territory — use it only as supporting context, not the central question.
